**Evaluation — Referee A item (3), structured environments:**

The referee asks whether the exclusion of structured environments is a limitation of the proof or of the physics. Our available results give a clear answer: it is a limitation of the proof. Assumption (A2) imposes a static Markovian environment. Oyelaran et al. (2023) demonstrate that real edge environments produce non-Markovian coherence revivals over the edge-transit window and that resonant fluctuators near the fusion-energy splitting enhance dephasing by up to a factor of twelve relative to a smooth-bath estimate. These are genuine physics effects our rate-equation framework cannot capture — not because the P1–P3 decomposition is wrong, but because the proof's structure (rates generated from a memoryless bath) is the wrong tool for that regime. The existing caveat sentence in 3.3 already correctly states that driven couplings and structured environments are outside the classification. The revision adds explicit references so the reader knows where to go when (A2) is suspect.

**Response paragraph** (saved as draft_0014 for your review):

> It is a limitation of the proof, not a claim about the physics. Assumption (A2) — that the environment is static and Markovian — is an explicit modelling assumption of Section 2.1, and the classification of Section 3 is exhaustive only within that model. The proof decomposes an arbitrary coupling operator under the assumption that the bath has no memory; when the bath retains memory (non-Markovian edge dynamics) or contains resonant structure (two-level fluctuators, phonon resonances), the rate-equation structure of the proof no longer applies, and effects outside the P1–P3 classification can arise.
>
> We have revised Section 3.3 to state this more precisely. The revised passage reads:
>
> "We emphasize that the monotonic decay of channel coherence under P1-P3 is a consequence of assumption (A2): the environment is static and memoryless, so information that leaves the fusion space never returns. Driven couplings and structured environments are outside the classification as stated, and we make no claim about them here. Readers interested in non-Markovian edge dynamics and resonant fluctuator effects — which can produce coherence revivals and order-of-magnitude dephasing enhancements absent from a Markovian rate treatment — are directed to Oyelaran, Salgado & Lin (PRX Quantum 4, 040318) and Nakamura & Chandrasekhar (arXiv 2610.09147)."
